To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fibrosis stage of alcoholic liver disease is not accurately determined using the current noninvasive tests, and that there is a need for a more accurate method for staging fibrosis.

the combination of fibrosis markers, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) to platelet ratio index (APRI) and fibrosis-4 (FIB-4), has a good diagnostic accuracy for staging fibrosis in patients without cirrhosis and with alcoholic liver disease.

the value of the FibroTest is limited for staging of liver fibrosis in alcoholics.
the use of fibrosis markers in patients with precirotic alcoholic liver disease is not useful to stage liver fibrosis.
the value of fibrosis markers in staging fibrosis in patients who have ALD has yet to be established.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the noninvasive markers of liver fibrosis (Fibrotest) is a useful tool for the assessment of liver fibrosis in alcoholic patients with a low to moderate alcohol consumption.
we have developed an approach for identifying patients with advanced liver disease, and in particular those with cirrhosis, using a noninvasive approach.

the combination of fibrosis markers and the clinical score (the BCLC score, which includes the presence of varices, ascites, and encephalopathy) is better than the fibrosis markers alone for predicting survival.
